links.comparator_used: Insecure agent workflow with undefended inputs, including client-side prompt construction, compared with the TRiSM-guided workflow
links.outcome: Attack success rate across RAG poisoning, data-field injection and client-side network injection (500 attack scenarios, 5 LLMs)
links.effect: Mean attack success fell from 31% to 10% for RAG poisoning and from 42% to 25% for data-field injection. The network injection vector was eliminated through server-side prompt construction.
links.quote: The TRiSM-guided agentic workflow reduced mean attack success rates from 31% to 10% for RAG poisoning and from 42% to 25% for data-field injection, while eliminating the network injection vector entirely through server-side prompt construction.

links.comparator_used: Insecure agent workflow in which agents have access rights exceeding those of ordinary users
links.outcome: Security (attack success rate) and report accuracy of the least-privilege, defence-in-depth agentic workflow
links.effect: Attack success fell from 31% to 10% (RAG poisoning) and from 42% to 25% (data-field injection). Report accuracy rose 14 percentage points, from 72.5% to 86.5%.
links.tradeoff: Model choice was highlighted as a necessary architectural consideration, which suggests results varied across LLMs.
links.quote: Furthermore, report accuracy increased by 14 percentage points (72.5% to 86.5%) with the agentic workflow, demonstrating a secure design which provides more reliable outputs.

design_hint: TRiSM-guided least-privilege secure agentic workflow (defence in depth, server-side prompt construction)
